newsitem.title: GERMANY: Study proposes Alpine Transrapid - magazine.
newsitem.headline: Study proposes Alpine Transrapid - magazine.

text.p: German steel and machinery group Thyssen AG has released a study showing a high-speed freight rail link through the Alps would be more economical than building the 250-kilometre tunnel now under consideration, the news weekly Focus reported on Monday.

A magnetic-levitation train for freight would cost half as much and could be built in half the time needed for the Brenner tunnel, concluded Thyssen, a partner in Germany's Transrapid developmental rail project.

Thyssen Industrie AG chief executive Eckhard Rohkamm told Focus the Bavarian government reacted positively to its finding that the Transrapid rail line between Kufstein, Austria, and Trento, Italy, would cost 14.2 billion marks over 10 years.

The Brenner tunnel was expected to cost 28 billion marks and require 20 years to build. Germany, Austria and Italy have already signed an agreement to build the tunnel to ease mounting traffic through the Alps, but have not agreed a financing plan.
Rohkamm said government and private investors could finance a Transrapid freight line, or the link could become a stock company itself.

The Transrapid consortium has sought to build a passenger line between Hamburg and Berlin, but opponents say it would cost too much. The group includes Siemens AG and ADtranz, a venture between Daimler-Benz AG and Swiss-Swedish group ABB.
